For most people, a power station with about 1,000–2,000 Wh of capacity and an inverter that can surge to at least 1,200 W will keep a fridge running through an outage. I read only one of the three guides, HomeGridHQ's. I couldn't open the Anker and powerstations.reviews pages because they were too large to load, so these figures come from HomeGridHQ alone. They are its estimates, not measurements.

**The two numbers that matter** ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Surge (watts):** A full-size fridge draws about 120–180 W while running. Its compressor briefly needs roughly 1,000–1,200 W to start. Look for an inverter rated at least 1,200 W, and check the surge rating, not just the capacity.
- **Capacity (Wh):** The compressor cycles on and off, so a fridge averages only about 30–50 W over a day. HomeGridHQ assumes the compressor runs about 35% of the time, which works out to about 62 Wh per hour.

**Capacity versus runtime** (fridge door kept shut)

| Capacity | Approx. runtime |
|---|---|
| ~1,000 Wh | ~16 hours |
| ~2,000 Wh | ~32 hours |
| ~4,000 Wh | 2.5+ days |

**Things to watch**
- Units under about 500 Wh usually can't start a full-size fridge. Their inverters are often under 600 W.
- Per USDA guidance cited on that page, food in a closed fridge is safe for about 4 hours without power. A full freezer lasts about 24–48 hours.
- A mini fridge or chest freezer needs less. A mini fridge runs about 80 W with a 600 W start.
- If you also want to power a freezer, lights or a router, size up.

**Options from that guide**
- **Overnight to a day (~1 kWh):**
  - [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D7PPG25F), about $499, 1,070 Wh
  - [OUPES Mega 1](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DG8JQNS4), about $469, 1,024 Wh
  - [Anker SOLIX C1000](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C5C89QKZ), about $470, 1,056 Wh
- **About 1.5 days (~2 kWh):**
  - [EcoFlow Delta 3 Max](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/ecoflow-delta-3-max-portable-power-station-2048wh), about $879, 2,048 Wh
  - [Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DFG2WDQH), about $899, 2,042 Wh
  - [Bluetti AC200L](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac200l), about $899, 2,048 Wh
- **Multi-day (3 kWh or more):** [Bluetti Elite 300](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-300-portable-power-station), about $1,199, 3,014 Wh, about 2 days.

The prices come from the HomeGridHQ page, which earns commissions on some links, and they may have changed. Check the current price before you buy.

My suggestion is a 2 kWh unit if outages in your area are long or frequent. If they're usually just a few hours, a 1 kWh unit is enough. If you tell me your fridge's size and how long your outages usually last, I can narrow it down.

 What Size Power Station Do You Need to Run a Refrigerator?
 Verified October 2026  Manufacturer + DOE typical ratings. [Methodology](/about/)
 Quick answer: To run a refrigerator you need a power station with at least 1,200W of surge (to start the compressor) and about 1,000Wh of capacity to cover most of a day. A modern full-size fridge uses 100-200 watts while the compressor runs , surges to 900-1,200 watts at compressor start, and averages 30-50W over a day thanks to cycling. For backup sizing, plan around 150W running, 1,200W surge, and a ~35% duty cycle. 
 Refrigerator wattage by type
 Type Running watts Compressor start 
 Mini fridge 80W 600W 
 Top-freezer 18 cu ft 120W 1,000W 
 French door 25 cu ft 180W 1,200W 
 Garage chest freezer 100W 800W 
 Refrigerators are the most common reason to buy backup power - a fridge holds $200-400 of food, and the USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed. The good news: fridges are cheap to back up. At a 35% duty cycle, one uses only ~62Wh per hour after inverter losses. Keep the door shut and even a 1kWh station protects your food most of a day. The number that disqualifies small inverters is the compressor start surge - clear 1,200W and you're safe.

 Computed from each unit's rated capacity at 85% inverter efficiency and a 35% duty cycle (150W running, 1,200W start). Units whose continuous output can't run it, whose motor-start surge can't start it are excluded. Where a maker's headline surge only applies to resistive loads, we size starts off continuous output.
